correctness.rationale: Uniform Motzkin paths have an exact first-return decomposition with mark for all horizontal steps and adjacent UD pairs, plus a separate mark at height zero. Differentiation produces six precise generating functions. The unique dominant singularity z=1/3 and transfer of half-integer singular powers through the third correction yields Cov(R,P)=-1/n+O(n^-2) and Cov(R,H)=2+O(n^-1). The exact amplitude/coefficients are checked by SymPy and finite path enumerations. These corroborate an analytic proof, not an inference of infinite behavior from finite tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2015 Motzkin polynomials give more general height-by-height horizontal-step enumeration, which can yield Cov(R,H) without the present proof. Their commuting height weights do not distinguish consecutive UD, although the same article also discusses a general noncommuting word enumerator that could in principle be specialized to every finite pattern statistic; no mixed sharp-peak formula or asymptotic covariance is stated. The 2005 peak formulas enumerate peaks and rises, not ground-flat/peak joint moments. Thus the first nonzero -1/n cancellation needs a joint derivation and singularity computation rather than being an explicit or immediate numerical corollary.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One-dimensional peak enumerators do not determine the joint peak/height-zero flat-step distribution. Conversely height-only commutative Motzkin polynomials do not distinguish UD adjacency: paths with identical height-step multisets can have different sharp-peak counts. Their conclusions thus do not logically supply the first nonzero covariance constant without further derivation. An analogous -1/n boundary covariance in permutations is on different combinatorial objects and does not imply this formula.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary prior work includes sharp peak enumerations (Sapounakis–Tsikouras and Brennan–Mavhungu), humps (Ding–Du) and height-specific horizontal step polynomials (Oste–Van der Jeugt). None of the materially inspected stated the joint ground-horizontal versus adjacent UD covariance or its first nonzero -1/n coefficient. Horizontal-only comparison is partially dominated by the 2015 polynomial and is contextual to the main new cancellation. Semantic prior-claim comparisons found no directly matching Motzkin result, and structural analogs in other objects do not imply this law. Historical priority remains uncertain because an earlier multivariate scheme might be specialized to the result.
residual_risks: Complete independent inspection of the 2010 Brennan–Mavhungu article was unavailable; its excerpted sections may have material beyond the inspected mean formulas.
General Flajolet–Viennot continued fractions or conditioned simply-generated-tree results could encode the coefficient implicitly, without presenting it as a covariance theorem.
Semantic database searches cannot establish global uniqueness or priority.

The 2015 noncommuting Motzkin word polynomial encodes all finite words, so exhaustive extraction can in principle recover finite mixed moments; this is a background enumeration rather than an explicit asymptotic covariance comparison.

value.rationale: The leading and constant mixed terms cancel, leaving a sharp negative boundary-to-bulk covariance -1/n. At the same time the covariance of exactly the same boundary statistic with total flats has a nonzero positive limit 2. The contrast identifies a nontrivial two-scale dependence distinction for a canonical random conditioned excursion, and the first nonvanishing coefficient supplies a quantitative benchmark rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
